verified_key_information_units.information: AS Tallinna Vesi reported strong financial performance in 2025 with revenue increasing 11.4% to €72.48 million, operating profit rising 11.8% to €21.22 million, and net profit growing 7.2% to €14.24 million. The company invested €55.74 million in fixed assets.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Main financial indicators table; Statement of comprehensive income

candidate_sentences.text: For the financial year ended December 31, 2025, AS Tallinna Vesi and its subsidiaries reported robust overall financial performance, characterized by significant growth in sales, operating profit, and net profit compared to the previous year.
Group sales reached 72.48 million euros, representing an increase of 11.4 percent, or 7.40 million euros, compared to 65.08 million euros in 2024.
Operating profit rose by 11.8 percent to 21.22 million euros from 18.98 million euros.

Net profit for the period reached 14.24 million euros, representing a 7.2 percent increase compared to 13.28 million euros in 2024, despite being impacted by an increase in the income tax rate on dividend payments.
The group continued heavy investments in infrastructure, investing 55.74 million euros in fixed assets during 2025 compared to 49.53 million euros in 2024.

verified_key_information_units.information: Customer revenue mix shifted significantly due to regulatory tariff harmonization: private customer sales increased 18.3% to €31.84 million from higher consumption, while business customer sales decreased 2.7% to €16.76 million following reduced tariff rates for businesses.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Sales section breakdown tables and text

candidate_sentences.text: Water services revenue grew by 6.9 percent to 62.31 million euros, driven by increased private customer consumption and tariff adjustments implemented across mid-2024 and 2025.

verified_key_information_units.information: Cost optimization and energy transition efforts reduced electricity expenses through the new combined heat and power plant at Paljassaare wastewater treatment plant, which supplied 43.8% of site electricity needs and increased renewable energy consumption to 87% of total energy use (from 23% in 2020).
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Energy use and energy consumption overview section

candidate_sentences.text: The financial performance was significantly influenced by operational efficiency measures, notably the full-capacity operation of the combined heat and power plant at the Paljassaare Wastewater Treatment Plant.
This facility successfully upcycled sewage sludge into biogas, generating 9,987 MWh of electricity and 6,933 MWh of heat during 2025.

This self-generated renewable energy covered all heat demands and more than half of the Paljassaare plant's electricity requirements, directly contributing to a 6.9 percent decrease in electricity purchase costs to 4.37 million euros.

verified_key_information_units.information: Infrastructure modernization advanced with smart water meter rollout covering over 80% of customers (targeting 100% by end-2026), construction of 45.1 km of pipes (49% via trenchless methods), and launch of trenchless sewer rehabilitation service by subsidiary Watercom renewing approximately 6 km of pipes.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Investing for the Future; Watercom activities

candidate_sentences.text: These investments targeted environmental protection, sustainable infrastructure continuity, stormwater systems, smart water meter rollouts, and treatment plant upgrades.

verified_key_information_units.information: The company achieved 99.5% compliance with drinking water quality standards and was awarded 'Green Company of the Year'. Environmental initiatives included constructing 7.1 km of separate stormwater systems to reduce flooding and setting ambitious climate targets to reduce Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions by 50% from 2020 levels by 2030 and achieve carbon neutrality by 2040.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Highlights from 2025; Sustainability Statement; Climate change section

verified_key_information_units.information: The group maintained a strong liquidity position with €11.29 million cash balance at year-end and €160 million outstanding loans carrying an average interest rate of 3.24%. In December 2025, €5 million was drawn under a €25 million loan agreement with the Nordic Investment Bank to support future investments.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Statement of financial position; Investors section

candidate_sentences.text: To support these capital expenditures and ongoing operations, outstanding loans increased to 160 million euros as of December 31, 2025, up from 118 million euros, including a new 25 million euro facility and drawdowns under a syndicated loan agreement.
Consequently, the total debt-to-assets ratio adjusted to 66.02 percent from 61.71 percent, while cash and cash equivalents increased to 11.29 million euros from 3.59 million euros.

verified_key_information_units.information: Tallinna Vesi continued its dividend policy of distributing 50-80% of annual profit, paying €0.53 per share (80% of 2024 net profit) to shareholders in June 2025, balancing returns with investment needs.

Key 2026 strategic priorities include completing the smart meter rollout, harmonizing water tariffs for residential and commercial customers by summer 2026, advancing the ozonation project at Ülemiste water treatment plant, reconstructing secondary clarifiers at Paljassaare wastewater treatment plant, and executing planned investments of up to €60 million.

details.completeness_justification: K1, K3 and K6 are fully covered. K2 and K4 are only partially covered because the candidate omits the core customer-mix shift and the specific smart-meter and trenchless-pipe metrics. K5, K7 and K8 are entirely absent.
details.coherence_justification: The candidate summary is internally coherent. Each sentence builds logically on the previous one: sales growth (S2) is broken down into water services (S3) and construction services (S4), followed by profitability metrics (S5–S11) that are consistent with the revenue increases. Explanations of operational efficiency (S12–S15) directly account for the cost changes reported in S16. Investment and financing details (S17–S20) follow naturally from the capital-expenditure narrative, and the unchanged provision (S21) is presented as a separate, non-conflicting item. No self-contradictions, logical gaps, or unnecessary repetitions are present.
